topic: ☕ Your 60-second sustainability coffee break is here. This week’s 4 highlights
text:
☕ Your 60-second sustainability coffee break is here. This week’s 4 highlights 

1️⃣ California’s packaging plan is now with CalRecycle

Circular Action Alliance (CAA) submitted its revised final draft SB 54 program plan to CalRecycle on Oct 13, 2026.

▪️ Submission is not approval.
▪️ CalRecycle has 75 calendar days to review the plan for compliance.
▪️ CAA’s schedule targets approval and program start on or before Jan 1, 2027.

2️⃣ Sharing one meter across many products

When a plant makes dozens of products, the allocation method used to split shared energy can change each product’s carbon footprint.

ISO 14044 sets this order :
 ▪️ Avoid allocation where possible
 ▪️ Use a physical relationship
 ▪️ Use other relationships, such as economic value

3️⃣ Organized packaging data supports smoother reporting

Seven US states have enacted packaging EPR laws : California, Colorado, Maine, Maryland, Minnesota, Oregon and Washington. Each program has its own scope, reporting requirements and timeline.

▪️ Organize data at SKU level, linking each product to its packaging components, materials and weights.
▪️ Document your estimates, data sources and calculation methods.

4️⃣ Clear documentation builds confidence in a carbon figure

A Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) report can cover the goal, system boundary, data quality, calculation method, uncertainty, limitations and review status.

🔗 The shared theme : Transparent data and well-explained methods help everyone follow the story behind a sustainability result.

topic: 🧾 Some customers ask for the report behind your carbon footprint figure. Is yours ready?
text:
🧾 Some customers ask for the report behind your carbon footprint figure. Is yours ready?

Stating kg CO₂e per unit is step one. Readers also need to understand the life cycle stages covered, the data sources used, and the assumptions behind the calculation.

👇 A Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) report can be structured around these 10 key sections :

1️⃣ Executive summary : Results, scope, and review status
2️⃣ Goal and intended use : Purpose of the assessment
3️⃣ Product and functional unit : Product assessed and reference quantity
4️⃣ System boundary : Included life cycle stages
5️⃣ Data sources and quality : Primary data, secondary data, and representativeness
6️⃣ Calculation method : Emission factors, allocation, and assumptions
7️⃣ Results breakdown : Emissions by life cycle stage and material
8️⃣ Uncertainty and sensitivity : How results may change and sources of uncertainty
9️⃣ Limitations and exclusions : Scope restrictions and data gaps
🔟 Review and document control : Review status, version, and supporting records

⚠️ Reporting gaps to watch : Undefined system boundaries, unclear data sources, undocumented assumptions, and misleading precision.

🔗 Traceability matters : Connect the reported result and its significant contributions to its supporting data, calculation method, assumptions, and system boundary.

📋 Explore all 10 PCF report sections and the checklist for reviewing your documentation.

topic: ⚡ Packaging EPR rules are evolving. Your packaging data needs a reliable foundation.
text:
⚡ Packaging EPR rules are evolving. Your packaging data needs a reliable foundation.

Seven US states have enacted packaging EPR laws : California, Colorado, Maine, Maryland, Minnesota, Oregon and Washington. Each program has its own scope, reporting requirements and implementation timeline.

Here are 3 common packaging data points to keep up to date 👇

1️⃣ 𝐏𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐰𝐞𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭
Record the material, format and weight of each packaging component. Keep packaging weight separate from product contents, and map materials to the categories specified by the applicable program.

2️⃣ 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐬𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞
Track the products you sell or distribute into each state and their associated packaging quantities. Use the reporting methodology accepted by that state’s program to calculate and report packaging supply.

3️⃣ 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐲𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐝-𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐚, 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞
Check whether the applicable program uses recycled content in its fee structure or other requirements. Where relevant, record the recycled-content information, retain supporting evidence and document your calculation method.

📦 Best practice : Organize packaging data at SKU level.

Link each product to its packaging components, materials and weights. This makes it easier to classify materials and aggregate data according to each program’s reporting instructions. Follow the specific program’s rules for permitted reporting methods.

📝 Document estimates, data sources and calculation methods. Review your records whenever packaging specifications or applicable reporting requirements change.

topic: ⚡ Same plant data. Different carbon results per product, depending on the allocation method.
text:
⚡ Same plant data. Different carbon results per product, depending on the allocation method.

Picture one electricity meter supplying multiple production lines while the plant makes dozens of products. Yet you need a carbon footprint for each individual product.

Here are 3 stages of the ISO 14044 allocation hierarchy 👇

1️⃣ Avoid allocation where possible
Check whether subdividing the process or applying system expansion can avoid the need to split burdens between products.

2️⃣ Use a physical relationship next
If allocation is still needed, partition inputs and outputs using a physical relationship such as mass or energy content, where it reflects how the flows arise.

3️⃣ Use other relationships last
Economic value is one option when a suitable physical relationship cannot be established or used as the basis for allocation. Changes in relative prices can change allocated results even when total factory energy consumption and production conditions remain unchanged.

🔎 Before choosing a method, group factory energy into 3 categories. Directly attributable process energy, shared process energy and general facility energy. Using one allocation basis for all three, without considering their differences, can make PCF results harder to justify.

📝 Document your chosen allocation method and why it fits the process. Clear reasoning and consistent application help reviewers understand and assess your PCF results.

topic: 🗓️ California’s final draft EPR plan is due to the state on Oct 13, 2026. What does it set in motion?
text:
🗓️ California’s final draft EPR plan is due to the state on Oct 13, 2026. What does it set in motion?

Under SB 54, Circular Action Alliance (CAA), California’s approved Producer Responsibility Organization, is scheduled to submit its final draft program plan to CalRecycle on Oct 13, 2026. 

Here are 3 things to know 👇

1️⃣ Approval comes next

Submitting the plan is not approval. CalRecycle has 75 calendar days to act, and CAA’s timeline targets plan approval and program start on Jan 1, 2027.

2️⃣ Funding starts in 2027

SB 54 requires $500 million a year for 10 years for the California Plastic Pollution Mitigation Fund. The total is $5 billion, beginning in 2027.

3️⃣ The 2032 targets

✅ 25% reduction in single-use plastic packaging and food service ware, against a 2023 baseline
✅ 65% of single-use plastic packaging and plastic food service ware recycled
✅ 100% of covered material recyclable or compostable

💡 Why it matters : CAA describes the plan as the roadmap for implementing SB 54. Its approval moves the program toward its Jan 1, 2027 start, and the program must deliver each of these requirements.

topic: 🚨 Four sustainability signals. One bigger question : Are you ready to turn them into better decisions?
text:
🚨 Four sustainability signals. One bigger question : Are you ready to turn them into better decisions?

⚖️ 𝐎𝐑𝐄𝐆𝐎𝐍 𝐄𝐏𝐑

On August 27, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon upheld Oregon’s Plastic Pollution and Recycling Modernization Act and lifted the preliminary injunction that had temporarily halted DEQ enforcement against members of the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW) since February 2026. On September 24, 2026, NAW filed a notice of appeal with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.

🏭 𝐒𝐂𝐑𝐀𝐏 𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐀

Net weight represents the material remaining in the finished part. Gross weight, yield, and scrap data help explain material input and production losses. Verify the material-input quantity and scrap calculation basis used in the PCF.

📦 𝐂𝐎𝐋𝐎𝐑𝐀𝐃𝐎 𝐄𝐏𝐑

In NAW v. Ryan, NAW challenges Colorado’s EPR requirements, arguing that the law makes Circular Action Alliance (CAA) membership a condition of selling covered products in Colorado. This is NAW’s argument, not a court finding.

🌍 𝐋𝐈𝐅𝐄𝐂𝐘𝐂𝐋𝐄 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐆𝐄𝐒

The GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard organizes product life cycle emissions into five stages : material acquisition and pre-processing, production, distribution and storage, use, and end of life. Contributions vary by product, and results depend on the defined system boundary.

💡 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐁𝐈𝐆𝐆𝐄𝐑 𝐏𝐈𝐂𝐓𝐔𝐑𝐄

Track each court case separately. Verify the basis behind every figure. Review stage-level results before setting reduction priorities.

topic: 🚨 Which lifecycle stage is actually driving your product’s carbon footprint?
text:
🚨 Which lifecycle stage is actually driving your product’s carbon footprint?

🌱 Some products may have a larger share of emissions in material acquisition and pre-processing.

🏭 Others may have production as a major contributor, especially with energy-intensive manufacturing.

🔌 Products that consume electricity or fuel during use may have a substantial use-phase contribution, particularly when they operate for long periods or require significant energy.

That is why a category average or general rule of thumb does not establish the actual lifecycle emissions of a specific product. 📊

The GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard uses five general lifecycle stages to organize product-level emissions in a Product Carbon Footprint :

📦 Material acquisition and pre-processing
🏭 Production
🚚 Distribution and storage
⚡ Use
♻️ End of life

The relative contribution depends on materials, manufacturing processes, distribution, energy or fuel requirements, expected lifetime and end-of-life pathway.

A total PCF shows the overall result. Stage-level results show where emissions occur and where further investigation or reduction work is most relevant.

Three practices support more reliable results :

✅ Define the unit of analysis (functional unit) and system boundary
✅ Document allocation methods and apply them consistently
✅ Test key assumptions such as product lifetime, operating conditions and energy source

⚠️ A cradle-to-gate result should not be directly compared with a cradle-to-grave result without accounting for the difference in included processes.

🎯 Calculate the stage-level results first. Then decide where to focus reduction efforts.

topic: ⚖️ Can a state make joining a private organization a condition of selling products there?
text:
⚖️ Can a state make joining a private organization a condition of selling products there? 

The National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW) says that's what Colorado's packaging EPR law does, and its federal lawsuit challenges the law.

📌 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠

🔹NAW filed the federal lawsuit, NAW v. Ryan, in July 2026.
🔹On Sept. 28, as part of its effort to gain a preliminary injunction, NAW submitted new documents arguing the state has not answered its main constitutional arguments.

🔍 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐰𝐨 𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐢𝐦𝐬 𝐍𝐀𝐖 𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐝𝐨 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐮𝐩

🔹"Membership is voluntary." NAW says Colorado characterizes membership in the Circular Action Alliance (CAA), the private organization that administers the state's EPR program, as voluntary. NAW says that is inaccurate because the law makes joining CAA a condition of selling covered products in the state.

🔹"The state controls CAA." Colorado maintains that its Department of Public Health and Environment controls CAA. NAW disputes whether that oversight satisfies the U.S. Constitution's requirements for a private organization exercising government power.

📝 𝐀𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐝, 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐍𝐀𝐖

🔹 That the state could meet its recycling goals with less burden on interstate commerce.

🔹 That the law's ban on listing EPR fees on invoices regulates speech. NAW says courts have ruled on similar bans and Colorado has not distinguished those decisions from this case.

🔹 That the state has not identified a compelling interest to justify requiring businesses to join and pay into CAA.

🚚 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐫𝐞

A core issue with EPR laws is that distributors do not design the packaging of the products they sell and have no control over state recycling and waste management programs.

NAW believes Colorado's law treats some distributors as though they control both.

It says EPR fees will not change how products are packaged or disposed of and will instead raise the cost of doing business.

🏛️ 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

These are NAW's arguments, not court findings. The FEDA article does not report a ruling on the preliminary injunction request.

topic: 📦 Your BOM shows what ships. Your PCF may need to show what it took to make it.
text:
📦 Your BOM shows what ships. Your PCF may need to show what it took to make it.

✏️ A finished part on a drawing shows the material that remains in the product. That is its net weight, and it is a natural starting point for BOM data. 
Production records tell a second story.

Material is cut away during machining, trimmed from edges, removed during processing, or rejected after a quality check. It does not remain in the finished part, yet it was still sourced and processed before leaving production.

🏭 That is where gross weight, yield, and scrap data become important. 
Neither net weight nor gross weight is automatically the right number for every PCF calculation. 

🔍 The relevant quantity depends on the defined system boundary, manufacturing process, available data, and accounting methodology. 

One detail deserves extra attention :

⚖️ A scrap rate based on gross weight is different from scrap expressed against net weight.

Using the same percentage without checking its calculation basis changes the material input result.

A stronger PCF data process connects :

🧾 BOM net weight
⚙️ Gross weight or material input
📈 Yield and scrap
🧮 Scrap calculation basis
🗂️ Scrap treatment and supporting records

The goal is not simply to choose net weight or gross weight.

It is to understand which material quantity represents the defined product system and how that quantity is supported by traceable data.
